parts.title: A Metal Spoon SINKS. So How Does a Giant Metal Ship FLOAT? (Part 1) | Float or Sink
parts.description:
A metal spoon sinks, but a giant metal ship floats. What is inside the ship? Be the air and find out! Part 1 of Primary 3 Science, Diversity of materials: the ability to float or sink in water.

In this part:
• Drop it in: a wooden block and a metal block, the same size (look closer at the tub)
• HOLD ON! Do heavy things always sink?
• Look closer: a window opens in a giant ship's hull
• Be the air: trapped inside a giant metal ship
• Look closer: a metal bowl floats, then sinks when water takes the place of the air
• Spot the hidden otter!

Key words: float, sink, trapped air.
Watch Part 2: raincoat or school shoe, which one soaks up the rain? Last episode: snap it or bend it?

TheOneApp, Explained: Singapore primary science, made fun. Play along with Pip, Basil and Momo: show fingers to lock in, keep score on your hand, beat the Buddies!

Singapore Primary 3 Science (2023 syllabus): Diversity of materials: the ability to float or sink in water, and waterproof (Chapter 3, pp. 56–57; treatment, p. 54). Also fits US NGSS 2-PS1-2 (Grade 2 to 3).
Safety: water play is always with an adult. In this video an adult does every test. The wax is a cold block of shoe wax: no candles, no flame.
Try it at home: find one waterproof thing you wear or carry on a rainy day, and show someone at home.
Singapore and the US: at the coffee shop, coffee is poured through a cloth strainer: fabric lets water pass through, and that is exactly the point. The ships you see from East Coast Park are metal, and they float because of the trapped air inside. In the US (Grade 2 to 3): a wooden canoe floats on a lake, rain boots are rubber, and you test materials the same way: change one thing, keep the rest the same.

parts.title: Raincoat vs School Shoe: Which One SOAKS UP the Rain? (Part 2) | Waterproof
parts.description:
A plastic raincoat and a fabric school shoe. Rain falls on both. Which one does the water soak into? Be a raindrop and find out! Part 2 of Primary 3 Science, Diversity of materials: waterproof.

In this part:
• Drip on it: one drop on a raincoat, one on a school shoe (look closer with a magnifier)
• Absorb and waterproof: rubber, plastic, glass and metals
• Be a raindrop: you roll off plastic and soak into fabric
• Wax it: shoe wax on a fabric boot keeps the water out (look closer)
• Showdown: find the mistake in Basil's notes
• A chant to remember it all
• Spot the hidden snail!

Key words: absorb, waterproof, wax.
Watch Part 1 first! Next episode: see-through, blurry or blocked? Light and materials.
